minutes.headline: Committee tentatively ranks Turkey Hill/schools, Town Hall, and Ritter as the town's top three capital priorities.
minutes.summary: The Master Plan Steering Committee reviewed feedback trickling in from town boards (Open Space, APDC, EDC, Council on Aging, Capital Planning) and heard that the town lacks several statutory plans, including an unfinished emergency management plan. Most of the meeting was spent working through a member's memo inventorying every town-owned building, out of which the committee tentatively settled on school facilities, Town Hall, and the Ritter building as its top three capital priorities, deferring Brooks House, Eagle House, Teen Club, and Marshall Park for later ranking pending input from the superintendent. The committee set plans for a final public feedback session on October 22 and a short presentation to a special town meeting on November 18, and discussed how to advertise the session and how candidly to describe the plan's troubled two-year process.

budget_items.what_was_said: The town previously approved a roof repair at TC Pasios at a 2023 town meeting; the select board last night proposed a larger warrant article for the same roof.

budget_items.topic: Renovation vs. new construction cost per square foot
budget_items.what_was_said: A committee member cited an engineer's per-square-foot cost for full renovation versus brand-new construction, explaining why renovating is favored.

budget_items.topic: Turkey Hill renovation vs. new school estimates
budget_items.what_was_said: The school committee has an engineer's estimate for renovating Turkey Hill, contrasted with an earlier estimate for building an entirely new school.
The select board directed the Lunenburg Municipal Building Design Committee not to bring back a project of the scale previously rejected.
A member described the town's yearly capital improvement funding pool that projects compete for each year.

budget_items.topic: Hypothetical cost of a formal prioritized capital plan
budget_items.what_was_said: A member speculated what a consultant-produced prioritization document like the one being discussed might cost the town.
Combining Turkey Hill renovation with primary school playground/entry work and athletic field fixes was described as expanding the project's likely cost.

budget_items.topic: Storm water task force potential taxpayer cost
budget_items.what_was_said: A member noted the town's storm water task force has discussed a possible added annual cost per average taxpayer, to be weighed alongside building projects.
Water district customers were said to be facing a large capital cost for a PFAS treatment plant plus ongoing annual maintenance, cited as a competing pressure on the tax bill.

decisions.decision: Cancel the November 26 meeting, the Wednesday before Thanksgiving.
Hold the October 22 session at Smoke Stack instead of a regular meeting, and present at the November 18 special town meeting, skipping the meeting the week after.
Jerry will resend the edited minutes and the committee will revisit approval of the three outstanding sets at the next meeting.

Include in the master plan a list of required/expired town plans (master plan, open space & recreation plan, ADA self-evaluation/transition plan, hazard mitigation plan, housing production plan, comprehensive emergency management plan) and their status.
Ask the consultant (Ramy) at the Tuesday working meeting whether recommendations in the 2019-2020 Open Space & Recreation Plan have actually been implemented.
Proceed with drafting a prioritized list of town capital construction projects for inclusion in the master plan.
Move the Eagle House and Teen Club to the bottom of the building priority list.
Identify school improvements (Turkey Hill etc.), Town Hall, and the Ritter building as the top three capital priorities, treated as roughly equal for now pending further ranking.
Continue and finalize the project prioritization discussion at the next meeting.
Advertise the October 22 info session via the committee's Facebook page, a letter to the editor in the Ledger, mention at a select board meeting, and possibly a school district email/newsletter.
When presenting to town meeting, acknowledge the process has been imperfect without over-apologizing, and emphasize concrete plan outcomes.

what_happened.line: Committee tentatively named school facilities (Turkey Hill), Town Hall, and the Ritter building as the town's top three capital priorities, treated as roughly equal for now.
Committee voted to proceed with drafting a formal prioritized list of town capital construction projects for the master plan.
A final public feedback session was set for October 22 at Smoke Stack, followed by a short presentation to the November 18 special town meeting.
The master plan will include a list of the town's required and expired statutory plans, including an unfinished emergency management plan.

why_it_matters: This ranking will shape which capital project -- school building work, Town Hall, or the Ritter building -- gets first call on the town's limited capital funding pool.
Residents get one more chance to weigh in at the October 22 session before this list goes before a special town meeting vote on November 18.
